chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman Al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyas, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about two groups of the believers, one of them being the rebellious (bāghiya) and the other just ('ādila), and the just one defeated the rebellious. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not for the just group to pursue the fleeing, nor to kill the prisoner, nor to finish off the battlefield, nor to execute the wounded. And this ruling applies if no one from the rebellious group remains, and they do not have a faction (fi'a) to which they can return. But if they have a faction to which they can return, then their prisoners are killed, their fleeing are pursued, and their wounded are executed.'

key_terms.بَاغِيَةٌ: Rebellious group (those who rebel against the Imam or just authority)
key_terms.عَادِلَةٌ: Just group (the forces of the Imam or just authority)
key_terms.فِئَةٌ: Faction or group (a distinct unit to which the enemy can return/regroup)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for pursuing and treating prisoners of war when one Muslim group fights another?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential distinction between 'qatl bi-l-‘illah' (killing due to rebellion) and 'qatl bi-l-dhimmah' (killing due to captivity) in Shia fiqh, specifically addressing the treatment of the Khawarij or mutineers. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the leniency of not pursuing or executing the wounded applies only when the rebellion is effectively crushed and the enemy lacks a cohesive force to regroup; otherwise, full military measures are permitted to prevent resurgence. This ruling underscores the strategic necessity of total defeat in internal conflicts to preserve communal stability.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Al Minqary, from Hafs Bin Giyas who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about two groups of the believers, one of them rebellious and the other one just, and the just one defeats the rebellious. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not for the just group that they should puruse the fleers, nor kill the prisoners, nor attack the wounded; and this is when there does not remain anyone from the rebellious people, and there does not happen to be a group they can return to. So if there was a group for them to be returning to, so its prisoners would be killed, and its fleers would be pursued, and their wounded would be attacked’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman ibn af-Minqariy from Hafs ibn Ghiyath who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the two groups of whom one is rebellious and the other deals with justice and the latter group defeats the rebellious group. He (the Imam) replied, ‘People of justice must not pursue the fleeing ones, kill the prisoner or hurt the wounded. This is when the rebellious ones do not have a group around to whom then they can return, but if they have such a group, then the prisoners are executed, the fleeing ones are persued and the wounded ones are eliminated.’”
